auth.description:
Connect your Amazon S3 account using AWS Access Key credentials.

**How to get your credentials:**
1. Open the [AWS IAM Console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/) and go to **Users**.
2. Select your user (or create a new one), then go to **Security credentials**.
3. Click **Create access key** — copy both the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.
4. Make sure the IAM user has the **AmazonS3FullAccess** policy (or a scoped S3 policy for your bucket).

Using a non-AWS S3-compatible service (MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, etc.)? Set the **Endpoint** field to your service URL.

accessKeyId.description: Your AWS access key ID. Found in AWS IAM Console → Users → Security credentials.

secretAccessKey.description: Your AWS secret access key. Only shown once when you create the access key.

endpoint.description: Leave blank for Amazon S3. Only set when using MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, etc.

bucket.description: The name of your S3 bucket (e.g. "my-company-files").

roleArn.description: The ARN of the IAM role to assume (e.g. arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/MyRole).

bucket.description: The name of your S3 bucket (e.g. "my-company-files").

file.description: The file to upload to S3.

fileName.description: The name to save the file as in S3 (e.g. "report-2024.csv"). If left blank, a unique name is generated automatically.

acl.description: Who can access this file after upload. Use "Private" for internal files, "Public Read" to make the file publicly accessible via URL.

options.label: Public Read/Write (anyone can view and upload)

type.description: Content Type of the uploaded file, if not set the API will try to figure out the content type.

aiMetadata.description: Uploads a file to the configured S3 bucket, optionally setting a destination filename, content type, and canned ACL (e.g. private vs. public-read). Use to store new content in S3. Not idempotent: when no filename is given a unique timestamp-based key is generated, so each call writes a new object.

read-file.name: read-file
read-file.description: Read a file from S3 to use it in other steps

key.description: The full path to the file within your S3 bucket (e.g. "documents/report.csv" or "myfile.txt"). This is also called the S3 "key".

aiMetadata.description: Downloads a single object from the configured S3 bucket by its full key (path) and makes its contents available as a file for later steps. Use to fetch a known file when you have its exact key. Reading the same key repeatedly returns the same content with no side effect (idempotent).

generate-signed-url.name: generate-signed-url
generate-signed-url.description: Generate a signed URL for a file in a s3 bucket

key.description: The full path to the file within your S3 bucket (e.g. "documents/report.csv" or "myfile.txt"). This is also called the S3 "key".

expiresIn.description: How long the URL should remain valid (in minutes).

aiMetadata.description: Generates a time-limited pre-signed download (GET) URL for an existing object in the configured S3 bucket, letting anyone with the link fetch the file without AWS credentials until it expires. Use when you need to share read access to a stored file. Read-only and idempotent (no object is modified), though each call returns a freshly signed URL.

generate-signed-upload-url.name: generate-signed-upload-url
generate-signed-upload-url.description: Generate a pre-signed URL that allows anyone with the link to upload a file directly to S3 without needing AWS credentials.

key.description: The destination path and filename inside the bucket, e.g. "uploads/photo.jpg".

expiresIn.description: How long the upload URL should remain valid (in minutes).

aiMetadata.description: Generates a time-limited pre-signed upload (PUT) URL for a target key in the configured S3 bucket, letting anyone with the link upload a file directly to S3 without AWS credentials until it expires. Use to delegate an upload to an external client. Generating the URL does not itself create or modify any object and is idempotent (each call returns a freshly signed URL).

moveFile.name: moveFile
moveFile.description: Move a File to Another Folder

fileKey.description: The full path to the file you want to move (e.g. "old-folder/report.csv").

folderKey.description: The folder path to move the file into (e.g. "archive/" or "new-folder"). The file name is kept the same.

aiMetadata.description: Moves an object within the configured S3 bucket by copying it to a new key under the destination folder (keeping the same filename) and then deleting the original. Use to relocate or archive a file. Not idempotent — the source object is deleted on the first successful run, so a repeat call errors because the source key no longer exists.

key.description: The full path to the file within your S3 bucket (e.g. "documents/report.csv" or "myfile.txt"). This is also called the S3 "key".

aiMetadata.description: Deletes a single object from the configured S3 bucket by its full key (path). Use to remove a known file. Idempotent: deleting an already-absent key succeeds without error, so repeating the call has no further effect.

list-files.name: list-files
list-files.description: List all files from an S3 bucket folder/prefix.

prefix.description: Filter results to a specific folder. Enter the folder path including the trailing slash (e.g. "invoices/" or "reports/2024/"). Leave empty to list all files in the bucket.

maxKeys.description: Maximum number of files to return (1–1000). Defaults to 1000. Use a lower number if you only need the most recent files.

aiMetadata.description: Lists objects in the configured S3 bucket, optionally filtered to a folder prefix (empty prefix lists the whole bucket), capped at a maximum count (1-1000, default 1000) and sorted newest-first. Use to discover files or look up an object key before reading, moving, or deleting it. Read-only and idempotent.

decrypt-pgp-file.name: decrypt-pgp-file
decrypt-pgp-file.description: Decrypt a PGP encrypted file from S3 using a private key stored in AWS Secrets Manager

key.description: The key (path) of the encrypted file in S3

secretArn.description: The ARN of the secret in AWS Secrets Manager containing the PGP private key

passphraseArn.description: Optional ARN of the secret in AWS Secrets Manager containing the passphrase for the private key (if the key is encrypted)

secretsManagerRegion.description: The AWS region where the Secrets Manager secret is stored (defaults to S3 region if not provided)

allowUnauthenticatedMessages.description: Allow decryption of messages without integrity protection (no MDC). WARNING: Without MDC, a malicious actor can silently modify the ciphertext, so the decrypted output may have been tampered with. Only enable this when working with legacy files where integrity protection was never used.

allowInsecureDecryptionWithSigningKeys.description: Allow decryption using a key not marked for encryption (e.g. a signing-only key). Enable this if your PGP key was not flagged for encryption use.

aiMetadata.description: Downloads a PGP-encrypted object from the configured S3 bucket and decrypts it using a private key (and optional passphrase) retrieved from AWS Secrets Manager by ARN, returning the decrypted contents as a file. Use when an S3 file is PGP-encrypted and you have the key stored in Secrets Manager. Requires the secret ARN for the private key; idempotent since it only reads and decrypts without modifying anything.

new_file.name: new_file
new_file.description: Triggers when you add or update a file in your bucket. The bucket/folder you choose must not contain more than 10,000 files.

markdown.description: Triggers when you add or update a file in your bucket. The bucket/folder you choose must not contain more than 10,000 files.

aiMetadata.description: Fires when an object is added or modified in the configured S3 bucket, optionally scoped to a folder prefix. Polls the bucket and emits each new or updated file based on its last-modified time. The watched bucket/folder must contain no more than 10,000 files.

de.\nConnect your Amazon S3 account to read:
Verbinden Sie Ihr Amazon S3-Konto, um Dateien in Ihren Buckets zu lesen, zu schreiben und zu verwalten.

**Wie Sie Ihre Zugangsdaten erhalten:**
1. Öffne die [AWS IAM Konsole](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/) und gehe zu **Benutzer**.
2. Wählen Sie Ihren Benutzer aus (oder erstellen Sie einen neuen), dann gehen Sie zu **Sicherheitsinformationen**.
3. Klicken Sie auf **Zugangsschlüssel erstellen** — sowohl die Zugangsschlüssel ID als auch den geheimen Zugriffsschlüssel kopieren.
4. Vergewissern Sie sich, dass der IAM-Benutzer die **AmazonS3FullAccess** Richtlinie (oder eine S3-Richtlinie für Ihren Bucket) hat.

Verwenden eines nicht AWS S3-kompatiblen Dienstes (MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, etc.)? Setzen Sie das Feld **Endpunkt** auf Ihre Service-URL.

Aktivieren Sie dies nur, wenn Sie mit alten Dateien arbeiten, bei denen der Integritätsschutz nie verwendet wurde.
de.Allow decryption using a key not marked: Erlaube Entschlüsselung mit einem nicht zur Verschlüsselung markierten Schlüssel (z.B. nur Signaturschlüssel). Aktivieren Sie dies, wenn Ihr PGP-Schlüssel nicht zur Verschlüsselung markiert wurde.

ja.\nConnect your Amazon S3 account to read:
Connect your Amazon S3 account to read, write, and manage files in your buckets.

**How to get your credentials:**
1. Open the [AWS IAM Console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/) and go to **Users**.
2. Select your user (or create a new one), then go to **Security credentials**.
3. Click **Create access key** — copy both the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.
4. Make sure the IAM user has the **AmazonS3FullAccess** policy (or a scoped S3 policy for your bucket).

Using a non-AWS S3-compatible service (MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, etc.)? Set the **Endpoint** field to your service URL.

pt.\nConnect your Amazon S3 account to read:
Conecte sua conta Amazon S3 para ler, escrever e gerenciar arquivos em seus buckets.

**Como obter suas credenciais:**
1. Abra o [Console de AWS](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/) e vá para **Usuários**.
2. Selecione seu usuário (ou crie um novo) e, em seguida, vá para **credenciais de segurança**.
3. Clique em **Criar chave de acesso** — copie o ID da chave de acesso e chave secreta de acesso.
4. Certifique-se de que o usuário do IAM tenha a política **AmazonS3FullAccess** (ou uma política S3 com escopo para o seu balde).

Usando um serviço não-compatível com AWS (MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, etc.)? Defina o campo **Endpoint** para o URL de serviço.
